questions.q: Where did the Spirit of Yahweh set Ezekiel down, and what was there?
questions.a: The Spirit of Yahweh set Ezekiel down in the midst of a valley full of bones.

questions.q: What question did Yahweh ask Ezekiel?
questions.a: Yahweh asked Ezekiel if the dry bones could live again.

questions.q: What did Ezekiel prophesy would happen to the dry bones?
questions.a: Ezekiel prophesied that the dry bones would have flesh and live again.

questions.q: What happened to the bones when Ezekiel prophesied to them the first time?
questions.a: When Ezekiel prophesied to them the first time, the dry bones drew together and flesh and skin covered them.

questions.q: What happened to the bones when Ezekiel prophesied to them the second time?
questions.a: When Ezekiel prophesied to the bones the second time, the Spirit came into them and they lived.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, who did the valley of dry bones represent?
questions.a: According to Yahweh, the valley of dry bones represented the entire house of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would do for Israel, which was represented by the dry bones coming back to life?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would lift the people of Israel from their graves and bring them back to the land of Israel.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Ezekiel to do with the two sticks?
questions.a: Yahweh told Ezekiel to write a name on each stick, Judah and Joseph, and then bring both sticks together.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say was the meaning of Ezekiel’s two sticks?
questions.a: Yahweh said he was joining the two branches of Joseph and Judah so that they would be one in his hand.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he was about to do for the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said he was about to gather the people of Israel on the mountains of Israel as one nation with one king.

questions.q: Who did Yahweh say would be king over the united nation of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh said that his servant David would be king over the united nation of Israel.

questions.q: According to Yahweh, how long would the king of Israel be their chief?
questions.a: According to Yahweh, the king of Israel would be their chief forever.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say he would establish with Israel, and for how long?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would establish a covenant of peace with Israel for eternity.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh say he would live forever?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would live forever in the midst of the people of Israel.

commentary.text: God restores dried bones to life. (Ezek. 37:1-14) The whole house of Israel is represented as enjoying the blessings of Christ's kingdom. (Ezek. 37:15-28)

Ezek. 37:1-14 No created power could restore human bones to life. God alone could cause them to live. Skin and flesh covered them, and the wind was then told to blow upon these bodies; and they were restored to life. The wind was an emblem of the Spirit of God, and represented his quickening powers. The vision was to encourage the desponding Jews; to predict both their restoration after the captivity, and also their recovery from their present and long-continued dispersion. It was also a clear intimation of the resurrection of the dead; and it represents the power and grace of God, in the conversion of the most hopeless sinners to himself. Let us look to Him who will at last open our graves, and bring us forth to judgment, that He may now deliver us from sin, and put his Spirit within us, and keep us by his power, through faith, unto salvation.

Ezek. 37:15-28 This emblem was to show the people, that the Lord would unite Judah and Israel. Christ is the true David, Israel's King of old; and those whom he makes willing in the day of his power, he makes to walk in his judgments, and to keep his statutes. Events yet to come will further explain this prophecy. Nothing has more hindered the success of the gospel than divisions. Let us study to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace; let us seek for Divine grace to keep us from detestable things; and let us pray that all nations may be obedient and happy subjects of the Son of David, that the Lord may be our God, and we may be his people for evermore.
